subject: a woman in her fifties wearing a maroon-and-mustard checked Chettinad kandangi cotton sari, crouched on her heels, drawing a pulli (dot-grid) kolam in white rice flour on a freshly water-sprinkled threshold

setting.place: doorstep of an old tiled-roof row house on a narrow street off the Kapaleeshwarar temple tank, Mylapore, Chennai, Tamil Nadu

lighting: natural available light for the time of day, plus one warm tungsten bulb spilling from the open doorway behind her; soft, low contrast

camera.shot: wide shot showing the woman, the full kolam and the house front
camera.angle: eye level from across the street

style: documentary street photography, natural film grain, realistic skin and fabric texture
avoid: coloured-powder rangoli (this is a white rice-flour kolam)
silk wedding saree, heavy jewellery, glamour makeup
jasmine garlands, oil lamps and marigolds piled in for decoration
subject posing or looking at the camera
North Indian elements such as mehndi or a dupatta

motion.subject_motion: her hand draws one continuous rice-flour line looping around the dots; she shuffles forward slightly on her heels; nothing else in the scene moves except a faint flicker of the doorway bulb
motion.camera_move: slow, steady push-in from wide to medium shot, no shake, no cuts
